title: Exceptional fibres over a smooth target are rational trees
statement: Let $V\subseteq K$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$ [def-weil-field], so for each $x\in K^\times$ either $x$ or $x^{-1}$ belongs to $V$. Suppose $K$ is separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed] and the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain. Set $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ and $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $W\to T$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], of pure relative dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with smooth generic fibre [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $f:Z\to W$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], an isomorphism on the generic fibre and between schematically dense open subschemes. Schematically dense means that $\mathcal O\to j_*\mathcal O$ is injective for the open inclusion $j$. Suppose $Z\to T$ is flat and finitely presented of pure relative dimension one and is semistable: the singularities of every geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] are ordinary nodes, with completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over an algebraically closed residue field $\Omega$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $x\in W$ be a point at which $W\to T$ is smooth, and suppose $Z_x=Z\times_W\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ has positive dimension. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] of $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field], and let $s$ be the composite geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to W\to T$. The reduced geometric fibre $B=(Z\times_W\operatorname{Spec}\Omega)_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme] is a nonempty connected nodal curve with finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components], each isomorphic to the projective line $\mathbf P^1_\Omega$ [def-sc-p1-standard]. Its dual graph, with one vertex per component and one edge per nodal intersection, is a tree (connected with no cycles). The set of intersection points of $B$ with the closure of $Z_s\setminus B$ in $Z_s$ has cardinality at most two. Neither $W$ nor $Z$ is required to be separated or proper over $T$; no stability or marking assumption is imposed.
